summary: Forest-fire lookout tower on Haeckel Hill north of Whitehorse, built 1954; current structure 1961; still a radio repeater site in 2026.

facts.design: Tower with living quarters for forestry personnel (current structure, 1961)

events.note: First tower. ExploreNorth has found no photo or description of it; a 1956 Whitehorse Daily Star report says it was built in 1954.
Hugh Birch listed as towerman from 1954 to 9 June 1956.
Harry Burnett took over the post on 16 June 1956, per the Whitehorse Daily Star.
Current structure. A 1961 Whitehorse Daily Star report describes a tower and living quarters for forestry personnel being built.
Vandalism in September 1991 damaged the tower and the ham radio club's repeater; the electrical and electronic equipment in the tower was destroyed.
Staffed in the 2014 season, one of six Yukon towers staffed regardless of fire risk.
Still used by Wildland Fire as a local VHF repeater and a UHF link to another repeater near Teslin.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: ExploreNorth gives 1954 for the first tower, matching the Canada's Fire Lookouts list it cites and a 1956 newspaper report. It gives 1961 for the current structure, matching the 1961 construction reports. Both years are kept as separate events.
The operator is named as the forestry division in 1956, federal Northern Affairs fire management in 1991 and Wildland Fire in 2026.

sources.title: Haeckel Hill Forestry Lookout Tower at Whitehorse, Yukon

notes_for_editor: Two sources only: the ExploreNorth guide (updated 2026) and a Canada Lookouts page that transcribes newspaper clippings from 1956 to 1991 (Whitehorse Daily Star, Whitehorse Star). The clippings are used as the page gives them; the original newspapers were not checked. No height is recorded: the sources give elevation (5,000 ft), not tower height. Coordinates in the brief (60.77556, -135.27722) were not checked. ExploreNorth says the ridge with four wind turbines is locally called Haeckel Hill, while the ridge it calls the true Haeckel Hill lies to the northwest across a valley. Confirm which ridge the tower stands on before using the brief's coordinates. The story uses the common name, which ExploreNorth also ties to the tower's history, so the text does not need to change. Second pass: the road distance is 14 mi = 23 km (not 22 km); the Kepke line now follows his full statement, which says officials will have to look seriously at security. The brief's 'Government of Yukon' wording does not appear in the fetched text; the 2026 source says only 'Wildland Fire'. A 1981 tender for a 'lookout tower cabin' on Haeckel Hill appears in the clippings and was left out because it is unclear whether it was new construction. The ExploreNorth page refers to a photo gallery (1995 to 2026), but no photo URLs or licences were in the fetched text, so no photos are recorded. WebSearch was not used for this tower.
